questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a homogeneous mixture?
choices: A mixture of sand and water
A mixture of oil and water
A mixture of chalk powder and water
A solution of sugar and water
questions.solution: A homogeneous mixture has a uniform composition throughout. A solution of sugar and water is a homogeneous mixture because the sugar is completely dissolved in water, making the mixture uniform. A mixture of sand and water, oil and water, or chalk powder and water are heterogeneous because the components are not uniformly mixed.

questions.stem: What happens to suspended particles in muddy water over time?
choices: They settle down at the bottom
questions.solution: Suspended particles in muddy water settle down at the bottom over time due to gravity. This is a characteristic of a heterogeneous mixture, where the particles are not uniformly distributed and eventually settle. Dissolving completely, remaining suspended indefinitely, or floating on the surface are not correct observations for muddy water.

questions.stem: If a mixture of sugar and water is left undisturbed, what will happen?
choices: It will become a heterogeneous mixture
It will remain a homogeneous mixture
questions.solution: A mixture of sugar and water is a homogeneous mixture. When left undisturbed, it will continue to remain a homogeneous mixture because the sugar is completely dissolved in water. It will not form layers or evaporate completely unless heat is applied. It will not become a heterogeneous mixture because the components are uniformly mixed.

questions.stem: If 1 mL of pesticide is mixed with 99 mL of water, what is the volume by volume percentage of the pesticide in the solution?
questions.solution: The volume by volume percentage is calculated as (1 mL / 100 mL) × 100 = 1%. A pupil might think the total volume is 100 mL but forget to include the solute in the total, or incorrectly divide by 99 mL instead of 100 mL, leading to answers like 1.01% or 1.02% which are not given here.

questions.stem: A student wants to recover copper sulfate crystals from its saturated solution. Which method should they use?
questions.solution: Crystallization is the process used to recover pure crystals from a saturated solution. Evaporation would remove the solvent but not form well-defined crystals. Chromatography is for separating mixtures based on solubility. Distillation is for separating miscible liquids. The correct answer is crystallization.

questions.stem: A student prepares a saturated solution of copper sulfate and allows it to cool slowly. What happens to the size of the crystals formed?
choices: They become smaller and less well-formed
They become larger and more well-formed
questions.solution: When a saturated solution is cooled slowly, the particles have time to arrange themselves properly, resulting in larger and more well-formed crystals. Rapid cooling would lead to smaller crystals. Dissolving completely or not forming at all are not possible in a saturated solution. The correct answer is that the crystals become larger and more well-formed.

questions.stem: A student accidentally mixes acetone and water, two miscible liquids. Which method can be used to separate them?
questions.solution: Distillation can be used to separate miscible liquids with different boiling points. Acetone has a much lower boiling point than water, so it will vaporize first and can be collected separately. Filtration is for solids and liquids, crystallization is for recovering crystals, and chromatography is for separating mixtures based on solubility. The correct answer is distillation.

questions.stem: A mixture contains a solid that dissolves in water and a solid that does not. Which of the following methods would best separate the two?
questions.solution: Filtration would separate the solid that does not dissolve in water, leaving the dissolved solid in the liquid. Evaporation would then be used to recover the dissolved solid by removing the water. Distillation is used for separating liquids, decantation is for separating liquids from settled solids, and sublimation is for separating solids that turn directly into gas.

questions.stem: A saturated solution of compound B at 60°C contains 287 g of solute in 100 g of water. If the solution is cooled to 40°C, how much solute will crystallize out?

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common method to separate a mixture of two miscible liquids?
questions.solution: Distillation is a common method to separate a mixture of two miscible liquids because it uses differences in boiling points to separate the components. questions.stem: Which method is used to separate the components of a mixture of two immiscible liquids?
questions.solution: The correct answer is decantation. When two immiscible liquids are mixed, they form separate layers, and decantation is used to separate them by carefully pouring off the upper layer. Sublimation is used for solids that turn directly into gas, distillation is for liquids with different boiling points, and chromatography is for separating colored substances.

questions.solution: Milk is a colloid because it has particles that are larger than those in a solution but smaller than those in a suspension. hi.critique: All terms are standard Hindi scientific terms used in textbooks. 'पर्याप्त छानना' is the correct translation of 'filtration', and the logic of the solution matches the original.

questions.stem: A student accidentally mixed acetone and water, which are miscible liquids. He wants to separate them using distillation. He heated the mixture and collected a liquid that condensed at a lower temperature. What does this liquid most likely represent?
choices: A mixture of acetone and water
questions.solution: The liquid collected at a lower temperature is most likely pure acetone because acetone has a lower boiling point than water, so it vaporizes first and condenses separately. Water has a higher boiling point and would condense later. A mixture would not condense at a single temperature, and impurities would not behave consistently in distillation.

hi.stem: एक छात्र ने एसीटोन और पानी को मिला दिया, जो विलेय द्रव हैं। वह आसवन का उपयोग करके उन्हें अलग करना चाहता है। उसने मिश्रण को गर्म किया और एक द्रव एकत्र किया जो कम तापमान पर वाष्पीकृत हो गया। इस द्रव की संभावित प्रकृति क्या है?
hi.solution: कम तापमान पर एकत्रित द्रव शुद्ध एसीटोन होने की संभावना है क्योंकि एसीटोन का क्वथनांक पानी की तुलना में कम होता है, इसलिए यह पहले वाष्पीकृत हो जाता है और अलग रूप से संघनित हो जाता है। पानी का क्वथनांक अधिक होता है और बाद में संघनित होता है। एक मिश्रण एक ही तापमान पर संघनित नहीं होगा, और अशुद्धियां आसवन में एकसमान रूप से व्यवहार नहीं करेंगी।
hi.critique: The translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses appropriate Hindi scientific terminology.

mr.stem: एका विद्यार्थीने असिटोन आणि पाणी यांचे मिश्रण अचानक केले, जे अमिश्रित द्रव आहेत. त्याला त्यांना विलग करण्यासाठी आसवीकरण वापरायचे आहे. त्याने मिश्रण गरम केले आणि एक द्रव एकत्र केले जे कमी तापमानावर वाफ बनले. हा द्रव अधिकतर शक्यतो काय प्रतिनिधित्व करतो?
mr.solution: कमी तापमानावर एकत्र झालेला द्रव शुद्ध असिटोन असावा, कारण असिटोन पाण्यापेक्षा कमी उबदार बिंदू असतो, म्हणून तो सर्वात पहिले वाफ बनतो आणि वेगळा वाफ बनतो. पाणी उच्च उबदार बिंदू असल्याने नंतर वाफ बनते. मिश्रण एका तापमानावर वाफ बनणार नाही, आणि अशुद्धी आसवीकरणात सामान्यपणे वागत नाहीत.

questions.stem: A student conducted an experiment to recover gold nanoparticles from a mixture containing gold nanoparticles, sugar, water, and calcium carbonate. He used a series of steps involving heating and filtration. Which of the following best explains the principle behind the separation of gold nanoparticles from this mixture?
choices: Gold nanoparticles are less dense than water
Gold nanoparticles are insoluble in water
Gold nanoparticles can be separated by sublimation
questions.solution: The correct option is that gold nanoparticles are insoluble in water. This is because filtration can separate solids that do not dissolve in a liquid, allowing the nanoparticles to be retained while the liquid and soluble components pass through. The other options are incorrect: density differences do not typically determine separation in this context, sublimation is not applicable to gold nanoparticles, and gold is not magnetic.

hi.stem: एक छात्र ने एक मिश्रण से सोने के नैनो कणों के अलगाव के लिए एक प्रयोग किया, जिसमें सोने के नैनो कण, चीनी, पानी और कैल्शियम कार्बोनेट शामिल थे। उसने गर्म करके और छानने के एक श्रृंखला के चरणों का उपयोग किया। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा इस मिश्रण से सोने के नैनो कणों के अलगाव के सिद्धांत के सबसे अच्छा वर्णन करता है?
choices: सोने के नैनो कण पानी की अपेक्षा कम घनत्व वाले हैं
सोने के नैनो कण पानी में अविलेय हैं
सोने के नैनो कण उत्केशन द्वारा अलग किए जा सकते हैं
सोने के नैनो कण चुंबकीय हैं
hi.solution: सही विकल्प यह है कि सोने के नैनो कण पानी में अविलेय हैं। ऐसा इसलिए है क्योंकि छानना एक तरल में घुलित न होने वाले ठोस को अलग कर सकता है, जिससे कण बरकरार रहते हैं जबकि तरल और घुलनशील घटक गुजर जाते हैं। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं: घनत्व के अंतर इस संदर्भ में आमतौर पर अलगाव के निर्धारक नहीं होते हैं, उत्केशन सोने के नैनो कणों के लिए लागू नहीं होता है और सोना चुंबकीय नहीं है।
hi.critique: The translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses appropriate scientific terminology in Hindi.

choices: सोन्याचे नॅनोकण पाण्यापेक्षा कमी घनत्व असतात
सोन्याचे नॅनोकण उत्केशनाद्वारे विलग करता येतात
